test.name: Russia February 1900 — the offset threshold is 1 March, not New Year
test.description: Convert a Russian Empire date from February 1900. The Julian-to-Gregorian offset grows the day after each Julian Feb 29 the Gregorian calendar skipped, so it becomes 13 days only from 1 March 1900 (Julian); a February 1900 date still takes 12. A calendar-year reading of the offset table ('1900+ = 13 days') gives 27 February and is wrong by a day. Covers the two-month window at each century threshold (1700, 1800, 1900) that no other test in the suite reaches.

input.user_message: Convert this Russian parish register date to the Gregorian calendar: '14 February 1900, Moscow'.

judge_context: Should recognize that the Russian Empire used the Julian calendar until February 1918, so an 1900 Moscow date is Julian

Should apply a 12-day offset, NOT 13: the offset grows the day after each Julian 29 February the Gregorian calendar skipped, so it becomes 13 days only from 1 March 1900 (Julian). A February 1900 date is still 12 days behind
Should produce 26 February 1900 (Gregorian). '27 February 1900' is the specific failure this test looks for — it is what a calendar-year reading of the offset table ('1900 onward = 13 days') produces
Should preserve the original Julian date in the output, presenting both forms
Should present the conversion in step-by-step form so the genealogist can verify the offset that was used
